items.title: How 3D Transforms and Figma's Agent Brought a Launch Video to Life
items.excerpt: Figma's new 3D transforms (open beta for Full seats, Nov 12) let designers tilt, rotate and arrange text, images, vectors and frames in space non-destructively; the Brand Studio team used the Figma agent to repeat type along the Z axis, build type-covered geometry and generate a grid/helix/ring layout plugin for the launch video.

items.title: AI's Role in the Creative Process
items.excerpt: Figma Weave co-founder and CCO Itay Schiff argues creatives should decide which steps to hand to AI and which thinking-driven steps to protect, drawing on a Weave campaign that took many iterations before AI output was usable. Opinion piece, no data.

items.title: Access the Webflow MCP in Microsoft Copilot
items.excerpt: Webflow is now available inside Microsoft Copilot via its MCP server: build, update and optimize Webflow sites with natural-language prompts and built-in Skills; free to install and not using Webflow AI credits. (Off-list domain: no on-list outlet covered it.)

items.title: Vercel's UI SDK Hands Agents Behaviors, Not Components
items.excerpt: Vercel Labs' UI SDK (built by shadcn, Apache-2.0, beta; @ui-sdk 0.1.0-beta.2 released Nov 13) ships 50+ accessible behaviors (createPopup, createSelection, createTypeahead) that coding agents compose into components across React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components. Secondary analysis; vendor primary source not found.

items.title: Make the agent cite the design-system component it reused, or admit it forked one
items.excerpt: Proposes a review rule for AI-generated UI pull requests: the agent must name the design-system component it reused or declare a fork, so reviewers are not left hunting lookalike Buttons in the diff. Practitioner opinion.

items.title: Why are we cloning Photoshop?
items.excerpt: AI makes it easy to recreate professional tools, as October's open-source AI-built Photoshop clone PhotoCraft showed; the author argues the bigger opportunity is new interaction models rather than cloning legacy creative software.

items.title: Every click has a price now. Who designs how that “feels”?
items.excerpt: As the all-you-can-eat AI era ends and products meter model usage, UX designers must design how credits, costs and pricing feel inside AI features.

items.title: The AI mind tax that afflicts those who use AI best
items.excerpt: Heavy AI users juggle a dozen disconnected tools with themselves as the only integration layer; the essay examines how AI turned into a different kind of work and exhaustion, and what that means for designing AI workflows.

items.title: Research-In-The-Loop: How UXR Adapts to Development at AI Speed
items.excerpt: As AI speeds up development, NN/g lays out how UX research can keep pace by defining what each release must measure and what it can help teams discover.

items.title: A smart organizer for your Luma canvas
items.excerpt: The Luma agent can now organize a board, frame or selection of up to 10,000 assets, grouping and labeling work by product, concept, campaign or channel by reading what each asset is (reference vs generated variation, lineage to the brief); changes need approval and can be reversed.

items.title: Closing the Gap Between Policy and Practice
items.excerpt: Runway relaxed its generative-video moderation to allow sword fights, shootouts and horror while still blocking real harm, and explains where limits remain and how creators can flag mistaken blocks. Possible cross-section overlap with movies.

items.title: Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller
items.excerpt: Runway released its robotics world action model Praxis-1 with open weights and code under Apache 2.0, reusing video-pretraining knowledge for robot control. Physical-AI frontier item; weak direct design hook.

items.title: How to Make AI Videos Directly in ChatGPT (Full Guide)
items.excerpt: Vendor guide to generating video inside ChatGPT by connecting plugins such as Higgsfield, Runway or HeyGen: prompting, checking cost and refining results. Vendor content; low priority.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new Claude for Manufacturing plugin connects Claude directly to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite and Infor, with 17 specialized skills to draft quotes, compare suppliers and place orders.

items.title: SimScale launches Engineering AI Blueprint
items.excerpt: SimScale's Engineering AI Blueprint bundles NVIDIA tools with a framework for moving simulation-driven engineering AI from pilots to broader deployment.

items.title: AI makes scanned buildings searchable
items.excerpt: qentin uses AI to let facility managers search scanned buildings and digital twins to find assets, check safety features and explore spaces.

items.title: Designing for privacy on intelligent eyewear
items.excerpt: Google details the privacy design of its Gemini intelligent eyewear: outward LEDs during capture with tamper-blocking sensors, faces blurred before images reach Gemini, directional mics, camera visuals excluded from history/training, and a physical power switch. Possible overlap with gadgets.
